findings.description: The instance user_data startup script embeds a static AWS access key ID (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA) and secret access key in cleartext. These credentials are stored in Terraform state, exposed via instance metadata/user-data to anyone who can reach the instance or read state, and are effectively non-rotatable.

The security group allows ingress on TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration of the portal_server instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts against the host.
The security group allows ingress on TCP/80 from 0.0.0.0/0. Combined with the instance's public subnet placement this exposes the web service as cleartext HTTP to arbitrary internet hosts.

The EBS volume attached to portal_server has no encrypted attribute, so the disk and any snapshots taken from it are stored unencrypted at rest, exposing data if the underlying storage is compromised.
The snapshot of the unencrypted portal_server_disk does not specify an encrypted attribute, so the captured volume data is stored unencrypted at rest.
The S3 bucket that receives VPC flow logs has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so network flow metadata is stored unencrypted at rest.

The subnet sets map_public_ip_on_launch = true, so any instance launched here (including portal_server) is automatically assigned a publicly routable IP, increasing the externally reachable attack surface.
The subnet sets map_public_ip_on_launch = true, so instances launched into it are automatically given public IPs and become directly internet-reachable.
